newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong down slightly, Bombay at three-year low.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong down slightly, Bombay at three-year low.

text.p: Hong Kong's robust share market lost some ground on Tuesday as investors consolidated their holdings after recent gains but in Bombay a lack of buyers sent the bourse plummeting to a three-year low, traders said.
Most major Asian markets finished the day lower.
Tokyo was off 0.21 percent, Bangkok lost 1.61 percent and Taipei was 0.66 percent lower. Jakarta, up 0.75 percent, was one of the few to rise.

Brokers said Hong Kong stocks, which finished down 0.45 percent, were lower as investors took a more defensive stance after a recent run of gains. But they finished well off the day's lows as some buyers cautiously picked up laggards.
The Hang Seng Index shed 61.30 points to close at 13,456.26 after reaching a low of 13,422.10.

"I think there has been some cautious buying during this period of consolidation," said Gary Wong, associate director at Vickers Ballas. "The futures have been trading at an 120-point premium to the index for the past two days. I think that is a positive sign."
Trade in Tokyo was volatile, brokers said.
The key Nikkei average's decline, which continued from Monday, induced some buying back in late trade, but the bottom side was still likely to be vulnerable, they said.
The key Nikkei 225 average ended down 44.13 points at 20,630.56.
"Slides in brokerage, banking and construction sectors didn't stop today," said Kenzo Doi, a strategist at Kokusai Securities Co Ltd.

"Weakness in the sectors had been offset by a rally in blue-chips, but they (blue-chips) couldn't support the market today," he said. Aggressive buying in some major global firms' shares had led the recent rally, brokers said.
Indian shares took a beating in nervous trade as the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark 30-share index shed 55.43 points, or 1.94 percent, to end at a provisional 2,796.
"There is a total absence of buyers in the market. It looks very bad..." said Kamal Kabra, former president of the BSE.
"Shares are down on low volumes. People are slowly leaving the market." Tuesday's fall erased the market's previous three-year low of 2,811.17 on November 19, 1993.
Bangkok's SET index slipped for the fourth consecutive trading day, down 14.82 points to 905.81.
Brokers said the fall was not linked to Tuesday's modest rise in November inflation but investors sold on persistent worries about the Thai economy.
"Thailand's slow economic growth was the key factor forcing investors, including foreigners, to sell shares today," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of Sitca Investment and Securities.
Late waves of profit-taking pulled Taiwan share prices down 46.42 points to 6,936.39.
Despite a bullish mood, brokers said a correction was needed after November's rally and further sharp gains since Saturday.
"Profit-taking was very heavy before the close and that may continue tomorrow," said Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment.
Overseas buying in Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) and a few heavyweight issues boosted Jakarta's market sentiment.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 4.64 points to end at 620.81 points.
At 1150 GMT the dollar traded at 113.95/00 yen and 1.5640/50 marks.
Gold finished at US$368.80/369.30 per ounce in Hong Kong, up from New York's Monday close of $368.00/50.
SIMEX Brent crude futures closed lower.
January settled at $23.48 per barrel, down 14 cents from London's settlement of $23.62.
